preamble: The palatalized alveolar fricative [zʲ] became the voiced alveolo-palatal fricative [ʑ] in Polish: the secondary palatal articulation merged with the primary constriction, which moved back from the alveolar ridge to the alveolo-palatal region. The change belongs to the same 12th-century development that turned soft s, z into ś, ź and soft t, d into ć, dź. Polish therefore has ź/zi [ʑ] where Russian keeps soft [zʲ]: zima /ˈʑi.ma/ 'winter', ziemia /ˈʑɛ.mja/ 'earth', ziarno /ˈʑar.nɔ/ 'grain', ziewać /ˈʑɛ.vat͡ɕ/ 'to yawn'.
phoneticEffects: Palatalization, Retraction, Change in Place of Articulation

examples.note: Old Polish ziemia is given as /ʑɛːmʲa/.

examples.from: Proto-Slavic *zь̀rno 'grain' (soft z before the front yer; cf. Russian зерно́)
